angular size.simpleMeaning: How big an object looks as an angle from your eye, like the Moon’s size in the sky.
angular size.contextMeaning: The angle size shows how large something appears from where you stand, regardless of its real size or distance.
angular size.translationJa: 目で見た時の物の見かけの大きさの角度。例えば月の角度のおよそ半度。
angular size.translationEs: El tamaño aparente de un objeto medido como ángulo desde el ojo, como el tamaño de la Luna.
angular size.example: Used in astronomy and perception research to describe apparent size independently of physical size or distance.

what is the moon illusion?.simpleMeaning: The Moon looks bigger near the horizon than high in the sky, though its real size doesn’t change.
what is the moon illusion?.contextMeaning: This is a visual trick; photos show the Moon stays the same size all night.
what is the moon illusion?.translationJa: 月が地平線近くで大きく見える錯覚。実際の大きさは変わらない。
what is the moon illusion?.translationEs: La Luna parece más grande en el horizonte que en lo alto, aunque su tamaño real no cambia.
what is the moon illusion?.example: The effect is entirely perceptual; photographs show the Moon's disc is the same size throughout the night.

perceived distance.simpleMeaning: How far away the brain thinks something is, which can be different from the true distance.
perceived distance.contextMeaning: Believing the Moon is farther causes the brain to see it as larger.
perceived distance.translationJa: 脳が感じる物の距離。実際の距離と違うことがある。
perceived distance.translationEs: La distancia que percibe el cerebro, que puede diferir de la distancia real.
perceived distance.example: Kaufman and Kaufman showed that when observers believed the Moon was farther away, they judged it as larger.

what did kaufman and kaufman conclude in.simpleMeaning: The brain decides size by how far it thinks an object is, not just by image size on the eye.
what did kaufman and kaufman conclude in.contextMeaning: A landscape at the horizon seems farther, so the brain makes the Moon look bigger there.
what did kaufman and kaufman conclude in.translationJa: 脳は見かけの大きさを距離を基に計算する。地平線の景色が遠く感じられ月を大きく見せる。
what did kaufman and kaufman conclude in.translationEs: El cerebro calcula el tamaño aparente usando la distancia percibida, haciendo que la Luna en el horizonte parezca más grande.
what did kaufman and kaufman conclude in.example: Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2000.

telephoto lens.simpleMeaning: A long camera lens that makes far things look bigger and closer together.
telephoto lens.contextMeaning: It lets photographers copy the Moon illusion by showing Moon and landmarks at similar sizes.
telephoto lens.translationJa: 遠くの物を大きく写す長いレンズ。月の錯覚を写真で再現できる。
telephoto lens.translationEs: Un lente largo que amplía objetos distantes y comprime la profundidad, recreando la ilusión de la Luna.
telephoto lens.example: A telephoto lens placed far from a landmark brings the Moon and the landmark to a similar apparent scale in the frame.

why do trees and buildings strengthen th.simpleMeaning: Trees and buildings help the brain judge size, making the Moon look bigger near them.
why do trees and buildings strengthen th.contextMeaning: They give size clues that don’t exist when the Moon is high in the sky, so the brain scales the Moon up near the horizon.
why do trees and buildings strengthen th.translationJa: 木や建物が大きさの基準となり、月をあたかも大きく見せる。
why do trees and buildings strengthen th.translationEs: Los árboles y edificios son referencias que hacen que la Luna parezca más grande cerca de ellos.
why do trees and buildings strengthen th.example: Overhead, there are no reference objects, so the brain does not scale the Moon up.

what is the flattened-sky theory of the.simpleMeaning: People see the sky as a flat dome, so the horizon feels farther and objects there look bigger.
what is the flattened-sky theory of the.contextMeaning: This idea explains the Moon illusion alongside the brain’s distance scaling.
what is the flattened-sky theory of the.translationJa: 空を平らに感じ、地平線が遠く見え、物が大きく見える理論。
what is the flattened-sky theory of the.reading: うちゅうへいかんせい
what is the flattened-sky theory of the.translationEs: Las personas perciben el cielo como un domo plano; el horizonte parece más lejano y los objetos allí se ven más grandes.
what is the flattened-sky theory of the.example: This theory works alongside the apparent-distance theory to explain why the horizon moon looks larger.

why doesn't a wide-angle camera show the.simpleMeaning: Wide-angle cameras show the real size of the Moon, without the brain’s size tricks.
why doesn't a wide-angle camera show the.contextMeaning: Only a telephoto lens with a distant object can copy the Moon illusion in photos.
why doesn't a wide-angle camera show the.translationJa: 広角レンズは実際の月の大きさを写し、錯覚は映らない。
why doesn't a wide-angle camera show the.translationEs: Una cámara gran angular muestra el tamaño real de la Luna sin la escala perceptual del cerebro.
why doesn't a wide-angle camera show the.example: Photographers need a telephoto lens and a distant landmark to recreate the illusion in a photograph.

illusion.simpleMeaning: An illusion is when something looks different from what it really is.
illusion.contextMeaning: Here, 'Moon illusion' means the Moon appears bigger near the horizon even though it isn't.
illusion.translationJa: この文脈で「illusion」とは、月が地平線の近くで大きく見える現象のことです。
illusion.translationEs: Aquí, "illusion" se refiere a que la Luna parece más grande cerca del horizonte, aunque no lo sea.
illusion.example: Scientists call this the Moon illusion, and its true cause has been debated for centuries.

sky.simpleMeaning: The sky is the space above the Earth where we see clouds and the Moon.
sky.contextMeaning: It means the Moon moves across the area above the Earth.
sky.translationJa: この文脈の「sky」は、月が移動する地球の上の空間を指します。
sky.translationEs: Aquí, "sky" es el espacio sobre la Tierra donde vemos la Luna moverse.
sky.example: The Moon does not change size as it crosses the sky.

larger.contextMeaning: Near the horizon, the Moon looks much bigger than when it is above your head.
larger.translationJa: 「larger」とは、もっと大きいことを意味し、ここでは地平線の近くの月が頭上より大きく見えることです。
larger.translationEs: "Larger" significa más grande; aquí, la Luna parece más grande cerca del horizonte que cuando está arriba.
larger.example: Yet near the horizon it looks dramatically larger than it does overhead.

overhead.simpleMeaning: Overhead means directly above your head.
overhead.contextMeaning: It refers to the position of the Moon high above in the sky.
overhead.translationJa: 「overhead」は頭の真上のこと、この文脈では空の高い位置の月を指します。
overhead.translationEs: "Overhead" significa justo sobre tu cabeza; aquí refiere a la Luna en lo alto del cielo.
overhead.example: Yet near the horizon it looks dramatically larger than it does overhead.

theory.simpleMeaning: A theory is an idea that explains how or why something happens.
theory.contextMeaning: The sentence talks about two scientific ideas explaining the Moon illusion.
theory.translationJa: 「theory」とは、物事の原因や仕組みを説明する考えのことです。
theory.translationEs: Una "theory" es una idea que explica cómo o por qué ocurre algo.
theory.example: Researchers have proposed many explanations over the centuries, but modern science points to two complementary mechanisms: the flattened-sky theory and the apparent-distance theory.

apparent.simpleMeaning: Apparent means how something seems or looks.
apparent.contextMeaning: Means the 'distance' that looks like it is there, even if not exact.
apparent.translationJa: 「apparent」は見た目や感じられる様子、ここでは見かけの距離の意味です。
apparent.translationEs: "Apparent" significa cómo algo parece o se ve.
apparent.example: Researchers have proposed many explanations over the centuries, but modern science points to two complementary mechanisms: the flattened-sky theory and the apparent-distance theory.

distant.contextMeaning: It means the object is far from the observer's point of view.
distant.translationJa: 「distant」は遠く離れていることを意味します。
distant.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

flattened.simpleMeaning: Flattened means made flat or less curved.
flattened.contextMeaning: Here it describes the sky as seen less curved than a dome.
flattened.translationJa: 「flattened」は平らにされた、または丸みが少ないことを意味します。
flattened.translationEs: "Flattened" significa algo menos curvado o más plano.
flattened.example: Researchers have proposed many explanations over the centuries, but modern science points to two complementary mechanisms: the flattened-sky theory and the apparent-distance theory.

frame.simpleMeaning: Frame means to make a border or shape around something to focus on it.
frame.contextMeaning: Forming a circle with fingers to look at the Moon inside it.
frame.translationJa: 「frame」は何かの周りを囲んで注目すること、この場合は指で丸を作ることです。
frame.translationEs: "Frame" significa crear un borde para enfocar algo, aquí usando los dedos para enmarcar la Luna.
frame.example: One simple test: form a small circle with your finger and thumb, hold it at arm's length, and use it to frame the Moon near the horizon.

landmark.simpleMeaning: A landmark is a well-known place or important study.
landmark.contextMeaning: Here, it refers to an important scientific study.
landmark.translationJa: この文脈の「landmark」は重要な研究や場所を意味します。
landmark.translationEs: Un "landmark" es un lugar o estudio importante o conocido.
landmark.example: In a landmark study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, Lloyd Kaufman and James Kaufman tested observers using adjustable artificial moons.

lens.simpleMeaning: A lens is a part of a camera that focuses light to make a clear picture.
lens.contextMeaning: Here, the camera lens takes photos showing the real size of the Moon.
lens.translationJa: 「lens」はカメラの部品で光を集めて写真を撮るものです。
lens.translationEs: Una "lens" es la parte de una cámara que enfoca la luz para hacer una foto.
lens.example: Because a camera lens measures light physically rather than through a human perceptual system, a standard wide-angle photo of the Moon near the horizon captures it at its true angular size — small, often disappointingly so.

angle.simpleMeaning: Angle means the space between two lines or directions.
angle.contextMeaning: The size the Moon takes in your eye is an angle measurement.
angle.translationJa: 「angle」は線や方向の間の角度のことです。
angle.translationEs: Un "angle" es el espacio entre dos líneas o direcciones.
angle.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

angular.simpleMeaning: Angular relates to an angle or measurement of size seen from a point.
angular.contextMeaning: Describes the Moon's size as measured by angle from the eye.
angular.translationJa: 「angular」は角度に関することで、ここでは目から見た月の大きさを表します。
angular.translationEs: "Angular" se refiere a algo relacionado con el ángulo o tamaño visto desde un punto.
angular.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

arm.simpleMeaning: Arm is the part of the body from shoulder to hand.
arm.contextMeaning: Move your arm to hold fingers in front of your eye to measure Moon size.
arm.translationJa: 「arm」は肩から手までの腕の部分です。
arm.translationEs: "Arm" es la parte del cuerpo desde el hombro hasta la mano.
arm.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

eye.simpleMeaning: Eye is the organ used to see.
eye.contextMeaning: The Moon's size is measured by the angle it takes up in your eye.
eye.translationJa: 「eye」は見るための器官のことです。
eye.translationEs: "Eye" es el órgano que usamos para ver.
eye.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

farther.simpleMeaning: Farther means more far away in distance.
farther.contextMeaning: Here, the horizon seems farther away than the point above your head.
farther.translationJa: 「farther」はより遠い距離を意味します。地平線が頭上より遠く感じられることです。
farther.example: The horizon feels farther away than the overhead point.

length.simpleMeaning: Length is how long something is.
length.contextMeaning: Describes the size of a thumbnail held out at arm's length.
length.translationEs: "Length" es la medida de cuánto mide algo.
length.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

moonrise.simpleMeaning: Moonrise is the time when the Moon appears above the horizon.
moonrise.contextMeaning: The Moon rising in the sky early in the evening.
moonrise.translationJa: 「moonrise」は月が地平線に現れることを指します。
moonrise.translationEs: "Moonrise" es el momento en que la Luna aparece sobre el horizonte.
moonrise.example: Its distance from Earth stays nearly the same from moonrise to midnight.

night.simpleMeaning: Night is the time when it is dark outside.
night.contextMeaning: Here, a single night refers to the time from moonrise until midnight.
night.translationJa: 「night」は外が暗い時間のことです。
night.translationEs: "Night" es el tiempo cuando está oscuro afuera.
night.example: NASA confirms that the Moon's actual distance from Earth changes only slightly over a single night — far too little to explain the dramatic size difference people report seeing.

observer.simpleMeaning: An observer is a person who watches or notices something.
observer.contextMeaning: The Moon illusion happens inside the observer's mind.
observer.translationJa: 「observer」は物を見ている人のことです。
observer.translationEs: Un "observer" es alguien que mira o nota algo.
observer.example: The effect is entirely inside the observer's mind, not in the sky.

perceptual.simpleMeaning: Perceptual relates to how we see and understand things.
perceptual.contextMeaning: The camera sees light differently than human perception.
perceptual.translationJa: 「perceptual」は見る・理解することに関係します。
perceptual.translationEs: "Perceptual" se refiere a cómo vemos y entendemos las cosas.
perceptual.example: Because a camera lens measures light physically rather than through a human perceptual system, a standard wide-angle photo of the Moon near the horizon captures it at its true angular size — small, often disappointingly so.

photograph.simpleMeaning: Photograph means to take a picture with a camera.
photograph.contextMeaning: Taking photos of the Moon at different times.
photograph.translationJa: 「photograph」はカメラで写真を撮ることです。
photograph.translationEs: "Photograph" significa tomar una foto con una cámara.
photograph.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

reference.simpleMeaning: Reference means something used to compare or measure against.
reference.contextMeaning: Here, objects near the horizon help judge size and distance.
reference.translationJa: 「reference」は比較や測定のための基準のことです。
reference.translationEs: "Reference" es algo usado para comparar o medir.
reference.example: Overhead, there are no such reference objects.

upward.simpleMeaning: Upward means moving or directed towards above.
upward.contextMeaning: The Moon near the horizon causes the brain to see it as bigger.
upward.translationJa: 「upward」は上方向への動きを意味します。
upward.example: The Moon near the horizon triggers this upward scaling.

actual.simpleMeaning: Actual means real or true, not imagined.
actual.contextMeaning: The Moon's real distance changes only a little during the night.
actual.translationJa: 「actual」は実際の、本当のという意味です。
actual.example: NASA confirms that the Moon's actual distance from Earth changes only slightly over a single night — far too little to explain the dramatic size difference people report seeing.

adjustable.simpleMeaning: Adjustable means able to be changed or moved to fit need.
adjustable.contextMeaning: They used fake moons that can change size for tests.
adjustable.translationJa: 「adjustable」は調整できることを意味します。
adjustable.translationEs: "Adjustable" significa que puede cambiarse o ajustarse.
adjustable.example: In a landmark study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, Lloyd Kaufman and James Kaufman tested observers using adjustable artificial moons.

approach.simpleMeaning: Approach means a way to do or think about something.
approach.contextMeaning: Photographers use a special method to copy how the eye sees the illusion.
approach.translationJa: 「approach」は方法や考え方のことです。
approach.translationEs: "Approach" es una forma de hacer o pensar en algo.
approach.example: Photographers who want to recreate the illusion as the eye perceives it use a different approach.

artificial.simpleMeaning: Artificial means made by humans, not natural.
artificial.contextMeaning: Fake moons made for scientific tests.
artificial.translationJa: 「artificial」は人工的で自然でないことを意味します。
artificial.translationEs: "Artificial" significa hecho por humanos, no natural.
artificial.example: In a landmark study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, Lloyd Kaufman and James Kaufman tested observers using adjustable artificial moons.

believe.simpleMeaning: Believe means to accept something as true.
believe.contextMeaning: People find the Moon illusion very real and hard to doubt.
believe.translationJa: 「believe」は何かを本当だと信じることです。
believe.example: The illusion is strong enough that most people find it hard to believe.

believed.simpleMeaning: Believed means thought something was true before.
believed.contextMeaning: People thought the Moon was farther when setting size.
believed.translationJa: 「believed」は前にそう思ったことです。
believed.translationEs: "Believed" significa que algo se consideraba verdad antes.
believed.example: Participants consistently set the horizon moon larger when they believed it was farther away.

camera.simpleMeaning: Camera is a device used to take photos.
camera.contextMeaning: The camera lens takes real-size pictures of the Moon.
camera.translationJa: 「camera」は写真を撮る機械のことです。
camera.translationEs: Una "camera" es un dispositivo para tomar fotos.
camera.example: Because a camera lens measures light physically rather than through a human perceptual system, a standard wide-angle photo of the Moon near the horizon captures it at its true angular size — small, often disappointingly so.

captures.simpleMeaning: Captures means takes or records something clearly.
captures.contextMeaning: The camera records the Moon's true size in the picture.
captures.translationJa: 「captures」は何かをはっきり記録することです。
captures.translationEs: "Captures" significa tomar o registrar algo claramente.
captures.example: Because a camera lens measures light physically rather than through a human perceptual system, a standard wide-angle photo of the Moon near the horizon captures it at its true angular size — small, often disappointingly so.

change.contextMeaning: The Moon's size does not get bigger or smaller as it moves.
change.translationJa: 「change」は変わることを意味します。この文では月の大きさが変わらないこと。
change.example: The Moon does not change size as it crosses the sky.

closer.contextMeaning: An object near you compared to farther away.
closer.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

comparable.simpleMeaning: Comparable means similar enough to be compared.
comparable.contextMeaning: The Moon and landmark look similar in size in photos.
comparable.translationJa: 「comparable」は比べられるほど似ていることです。
comparable.example: When a photographer positions themselves far from a recognisable landmark — a skyline, a mountain ridge, or a famous monument — and shoots with a long lens, the Moon and the landmark appear side by side at comparable scales.

complementary.simpleMeaning: Complementary means that two things work well together.
complementary.contextMeaning: Two ideas explain the Moon illusion together.
complementary.translationJa: 「complementary」は二つのものがお互いをうまく補う意味です。
complementary.translationEs: "Complementary" significa que dos cosas funcionan bien juntas.
complementary.example: Researchers have proposed many explanations over the centuries, but modern science points to two complementary mechanisms: the flattened-sky theory and the apparent-distance theory.

compresses.simpleMeaning: Compresses means presses or squeezes together.
compresses.contextMeaning: The telephoto lens makes the Moon and landscape look bigger together.
compresses.translationJa: 「compresses」は押し縮めることを意味します。
compresses.example: NASA's guidance on photographing the Moon illusion explains that a telephoto lens compresses the scene: it makes both the Moon and the distant landscape appear larger relative to the frame.

compute.simpleMeaning: Compute means to calculate or decide by thinking.
compute.contextMeaning: The brain calculates size based on how far something seems.
compute.translationJa: 「compute」は計算したり判断したりすることです。
compute.example: Kaufman and Kaufman concluded that the brain uses perceived distance — not retinal image size — to compute apparent size, and that the filled landscape between the observer and the horizon makes the horizon feel more distant than the empty sky above.

concluded.simpleMeaning: Concluded means decided after thinking or studying.
concluded.contextMeaning: Scientists decided distance affects how big the Moon looks.
concluded.translationJa: 「concluded」は考えた後に結論を出すことです。
concluded.translationEs: "Concluded" significa decidir después de pensar o estudiar.
concluded.example: Kaufman and Kaufman concluded that the brain uses perceived distance — not retinal image size — to compute apparent size, and that the filled landscape between the observer and the horizon makes the horizon feel more distant than the empty sky above.

concludes.simpleMeaning: Concludes means decides or believes something after thinking.
concludes.contextMeaning: The brain decides the distant object must be bigger.
concludes.translationJa: 「concludes」は考えて結論づけることです。
concludes.translationEs: "Concludes" significa decidir o creer algo después de pensar.
concludes.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

consistently.simpleMeaning: Consistently means always or regularly the same.
consistently.contextMeaning: People always set the horizon Moon bigger when thinking it is farther.
consistently.translationJa: 「consistently」はいつも同じように、規則的にという意味です。
consistently.example: Participants consistently set the horizon moon larger when they believed it was farther away.

constructs.simpleMeaning: Constructs means builds or forms a mental image.
constructs.contextMeaning: The brain creates an image of the Moon as it looks near the horizon.
constructs.translationJa: 「constructs」は心の中で作り上げることを意味します。
constructs.example: The resulting image matches what the brain constructs when standing at the horizon.

crosses.simpleMeaning: Crosses means moves across from one side to another.
crosses.contextMeaning: The Moon moves from one side of the sky to the other.
crosses.translationJa: 「crosses」は横切る、行き渡ることです。
crosses.translationEs: "Crosses" significa moverse de un lado a otro.
crosses.example: The Moon does not change size as it crosses the sky.

cues.simpleMeaning: Cues means signs or hints that help understanding.
cues.contextMeaning: Trees and buildings help the brain judge size and distance.
cues.translationJa: 「cues」は理解を助ける合図や手がかりです。
cues.translationEs: "Cues" son señales que ayudan a entender algo.
cues.example: Trees, buildings, and hills at the horizon give the brain real-world scale cues.

debated.simpleMeaning: Debated means discussed with different opinions over time.
debated.contextMeaning: Scientists have talked about the cause of Moon illusion for many years.
debated.translationJa: 「debated」は議論された、意見が分かれたという意味です。
debated.translationEs: "Debated" significa discutido con diferentes opiniones por tiempo.
debated.example: Scientists call this the Moon illusion, and its true cause has been debated for centuries.

degree.simpleMeaning: Degree is a unit to measure angles or temperature.
degree.contextMeaning: Used here to describe the size of the Moon viewed from Earth.
degree.translationJa: 「degree」は角度を測る単位のことです。
degree.translationEs: "Degree" es una unidad para medir ángulos o temperatura.
degree.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

disappointingly.simpleMeaning: Disappointingly means in a way that causes sadness or dissatisfaction.
disappointingly.contextMeaning: Photos show the Moon as small, which may let people down.
disappointingly.translationJa: 「disappointingly」は期待外れに、がっかりさせる様子です。
disappointingly.translationEs: "Disappointingly" significa de una manera que causa decepción.
disappointingly.example: Because a camera lens measures light physically rather than through a human perceptual system, a standard wide-angle photo of the Moon near the horizon captures it at its true angular size — small, often disappointingly so.

disc.simpleMeaning: Disc is a flat, round shape like a circle.
disc.contextMeaning: The Moon looks like a circle when seen from Earth.
disc.translationJa: 「disc」は丸くて平らな形のことです。
disc.translationEs: "Disc" es una forma plana y redonda como un círculo.
disc.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

dramatically.simpleMeaning: Dramatically means in a very noticeable or extreme way.
dramatically.contextMeaning: The Moon looks much bigger near the horizon than it does overhead.
dramatically.translationJa: 「dramatically」は非常に目立つ様子で、ここでは大きさの違いを指します。
dramatically.translationEs: "Dramatically" significa de manera muy notable o extrema.
dramatically.example: Yet near the horizon it looks dramatically larger than it does overhead.

enlarge.contextMeaning: The method does not make the Moon bigger in reality.
enlarge.example: This technique does not enlarge the Moon.

entirely.contextMeaning: The Moon illusion happens only in the mind, not outside.
entirely.translationJa: 「entirely」は完全に、まったくという意味です。
entirely.example: The effect is entirely inside the observer's mind, not in the sky.

factor.simpleMeaning: Factor is a reason or cause that affects a result.
factor.contextMeaning: Nearby objects are an extra reason for the illusion.
factor.translationJa: 「factor」は結果に影響を与える要因のことです。
factor.translationEs: "Factor" es una razón o causa que afecta un resultado.
factor.example: A third factor can reinforce the illusion: nearby objects.

finger.simpleMeaning: Finger is a part of the hand used to touch things.
finger.contextMeaning: Use your finger with thumb to make a circle to look at the Moon.
finger.translationEs: "Finger" es la parte de la mano usada para tocar.
finger.example: One simple test: form a small circle with your finger and thumb, hold it at arm's length, and use it to frame the Moon near the horizon.

form.simpleMeaning: Form means to make or create a shape.
form.contextMeaning: Make a small circle with your fingers.
form.translationEs: "Form" significa hacer o crear una forma.
form.example: One simple test: form a small circle with your finger and thumb, hold it at arm's length, and use it to frame the Moon near the horizon.

framed.simpleMeaning: Framed means enclosed or surrounded by a shape or border.
framed.contextMeaning: The Moon fits inside the circle formed by fingers.
framed.translationJa: 「framed」は囲まれた、枠にはまったことを意味します。
framed.translationEs: "Framed" significa que algo está rodeado o encerrado en un marco.
framed.example: The framed Moon fits the circle both times.

guidance.simpleMeaning: Guidance is advice or instructions on how to do something.
guidance.contextMeaning: NASA gives advice on how to photograph the Moon illusion.
guidance.translationJa: 「guidance」は方法や助言を示すことです。
guidance.example: NASA's guidance on photographing the Moon illusion explains that a telephoto lens compresses the scene: it makes both the Moon and the distant landscape appear larger relative to the frame.

half.simpleMeaning: Half means one of two equal parts.
half.contextMeaning: The angular size of the Moon is about 0.5 degrees.
half.translationEs: "Half" significa una de dos partes iguales.
half.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

held.simpleMeaning: Held means kept or kept in a position.
held.contextMeaning: Thumb held at arm's length to measure size.
held.translationJa: 「held」は持っている、保持する意味です。
held.translationEs: "Held" significa mantener o sostener en una posición.
held.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

hemisphere.simpleMeaning: Hemisphere is half of a sphere or globe.
hemisphere.contextMeaning: Sky seen as a dome half above Earth called a hemisphere.
hemisphere.translationEs: "Hemisphere" es la mitad de una esfera o globo.
hemisphere.example: **The flattened-sky theory** holds that people unconsciously perceive the sky as a flattened dome rather than a perfect hemisphere.

highest.simpleMeaning: Highest means the top or most high point.
highest.contextMeaning: The Moon's position at its highest point in the sky.
highest.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

hold.simpleMeaning: Hold means to carry or keep something in a position.
hold.contextMeaning: Hold your hand at arm's length to frame the Moon.
hold.example: One simple test: form a small circle with your finger and thumb, hold it at arm's length, and use it to frame the Moon near the horizon.

identical.contextMeaning: The two Moon pictures have the same angular size.
identical.translationJa: 「identical」は全く同じという意味です。
identical.example: If you photograph the Moon at moonrise and again at its highest point, both images show a disc of identical angular size: roughly half a degree across, or about the width of your thumbnail held at arm's length.

judge.simpleMeaning: Judge means to decide or form an opinion about something.
judge.contextMeaning: People think the Moon is bigger near the horizon.
judge.translationJa: 「judge」は判断することを意味します。
judge.translationEs: "Judge" significa decidir o formarse una opinión.
judge.example: When the Moon sits low on the horizon, most people judge it to be noticeably larger than when it sits high overhead.

judges.simpleMeaning: Judges means decides or assesses something.
judges.contextMeaning: The brain decides the distance and size of objects.
judges.translationJa: 「judges」は判断することを意味します。
judges.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

low.simpleMeaning: Low means near to the ground or horizon.
low.contextMeaning: The Moon sits near the horizon, not high in the sky.
low.translationJa: 「low」は低い、地面や地平線に近いことです。
low.translationEs: "Low" significa cercano al suelo o al horizonte.
low.example: When the Moon sits low on the horizon, most people judge it to be noticeably larger than when it sits high overhead.

mechanisms.simpleMeaning: Mechanisms means processes or methods that cause something.
mechanisms.contextMeaning: Two scientific explanations for the Moon illusion.
mechanisms.translationJa: 「mechanisms」は仕組みや方法を意味します。
mechanisms.translationEs: "Mechanisms" son procesos o métodos que causan algo.
mechanisms.example: Researchers have proposed many explanations over the centuries, but modern science points to two complementary mechanisms: the flattened-sky theory and the apparent-distance theory.

midnight.simpleMeaning: Midnight is 12 o'clock at night, the middle of the night.
midnight.contextMeaning: The Moon's distance stays similar from moonrise to midnight.
midnight.translationEs: "Midnight" es las 12 de la noche, la mitad de la noche.
midnight.example: Its distance from Earth stays nearly the same from moonrise to midnight.

moons.simpleMeaning: Moons is the plural of moon, meaning more than one moon.
moons.translationJa: 「moons」は「moon」の複数形で、多数の月を意味します。
moons.translationEs: "Moons" es el plural de luna, significa más de una luna.
moons.example: In a landmark study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, Lloyd Kaufman and James Kaufman tested observers using adjustable artificial moons.

nearly.simpleMeaning: Nearly means almost but not completely.
nearly.contextMeaning: The distance changes just a little during the night.
nearly.translationJa: 「nearly」はほとんど、ほぼという意味です。
nearly.example: Its distance from Earth stays nearly the same from moonrise to midnight.

noticeably.simpleMeaning: Noticeably means clearly or easy to see.
noticeably.contextMeaning: People see the Moon as clearly bigger near the horizon.
noticeably.translationJa: 「noticeably」ははっきりと、目立ってという意味です。
noticeably.translationEs: "Noticeably" significa claramente o fácil de ver.
noticeably.example: When the Moon sits low on the horizon, most people judge it to be noticeably larger than when it sits high overhead.

observers.simpleMeaning: Observers are people who watch or look at something.
observers.contextMeaning: People who took part in the Moon study.
observers.translationJa: 「observers」は観察者や見ている人々のことです。
observers.translationEs: "Observers" son personas que miran o estudian algo.
observers.example: In a landmark study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, Lloyd Kaufman and James Kaufman tested observers using adjustable artificial moons.

occupying.simpleMeaning: Occupying means taking up space or area.
occupying.contextMeaning: The object fills the same space (angle) in the eye as another.
occupying.translationJa: 「occupying」は場所や空間を占めることを意味します。
occupying.example: When the brain judges an object as being far away but occupying the same angle in the eye as a closer object, it automatically scales that object up — it concludes the distant object must be physically larger.

perceive.simpleMeaning: Perceive means to see or understand something.
perceive.contextMeaning: We see the sky as flattened, not fully round.
perceive.example: **The flattened-sky theory** holds that people unconsciously perceive the sky as a flattened dome rather than a perfect hemisphere.

perceived.simpleMeaning: Perceived means thought or seen in a certain way.
perceived.contextMeaning: The brain thinks the horizon is farther away due to landscape.
perceived.translationJa: 「perceived」は感じられた、そう見えたという意味です。
perceived.translationEs: "Perceived" significa pensado o visto de cierta forma.
perceived.example: Kaufman and Kaufman concluded that the brain uses perceived distance — not retinal image size — to compute apparent size, and that the filled landscape between the observer and the horizon makes the horizon feel more distant than the empty sky above.

perceives.simpleMeaning: Perceives means sees or understands in a certain way.
perceives.contextMeaning: Photographers copy how people see the illusion with their eyes.
perceives.translationJa: 「perceives」は認識する、感じ取ることです。
perceives.translationEs: "Perceives" significa ver o entender de cierta manera.
perceives.example: Photographers who want to recreate the illusion as the eye perceives it use a different approach.

photographer.simpleMeaning: Photographer is a person who takes photos.
photographer.contextMeaning: A person who takes pictures with a camera.
photographer.translationJa: 「photographer」は写真を撮る人のことです。
photographer.translationEs: "Photographer" es una persona que toma fotografías.
photographer.example: When a photographer positions themselves far from a recognisable landmark — a skyline, a mountain ridge, or a famous monument — and shoots with a long lens, the Moon and the landmark appear side by side at comparable scales.
